subject: humanities
passage: Spelling in early seventeenth-century England was far from standardized, and the workmen who set type for printed books often followed their own habits rather than those of the manuscripts in front of them. Bibliographers studying the 1623 First Folio of Shakespeare's plays have turned this inconsistency into evidence. One compositor, for instance, tended to set "doe," "goe," and "here," while another preferred "do," "go," and "heere." <u>By tracking such preferences page by page, scholars have been able to assign much of the volume to individual workmen and to estimate how carefully each one worked.</u> The results bear on editing: a reading that looks like Shakespeare's own peculiar choice may instead be the signature of the man who set it.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It offers an example of the contrasting spelling habits of two compositors who worked on the volume.
choices.B: It establishes that most of the apparent errors in the First Folio were introduced by its typesetters.
choices.C: It explains why English spelling had not yet become standardized when the First Folio was printed.
choices.D: It shows how a pattern described earlier was used as evidence, preparing for the point about editing.

explanation.why: The earlier sentences explain that typesetters had their own spelling habits and give an example. The underlined sentence shows how scholars used those habits as evidence to identify who set each page and how carefully. The final sentence then draws the consequence for editing. The underlined sentence links the pattern to the point about editing.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The example of "doe" and "do" appears in the previous sentence; the underlined sentence describes how such habits were used.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The sentence says scholars can estimate each workman's care, not that most errors came from typesetters.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text states that spelling was not standardized but never explains why; the underlined sentence is about scholars' methods.
explanation.D: Correct. It explains what scholars did with the compositors' spelling habits, which leads to the final sentence's warning to editors.
